overview: What is genuinely new this period is the shift from model-centric capability papers to runtime-centric control papers. The strongest NEW cluster is security and jailbreak diagnosis, where papers are moving beyond leaderboard attack success into checkpoint-level failure localization, stateful defenses, and provenance guarantees for compound AI systems. Cost-constrained RAG synthesis and KV-cache and sparse adaptation remain important stable directions, but the gap reading has sharpened: both are increasingly about hard memory-bandwidth and latency ceilings rather than retrieval quality or compression in isolation. Dynamic LLM evaluation and agent runtime evaluation are still large, but the notable change is that both now treat reproducibility and hidden model dependence as first-order problems. Structured 3D scene priors appears to be stalling relative to the other clusters this week, despite its large base.

macro_patterns.name: Trust under hidden dependence
macro_patterns.summary: The dynamic LLM evaluation cluster and the agent runtime evaluation cluster are converging on the same failure mode: benchmark scores and verifier ensembles assume independent signals, but shared model lineage, contamination, and opaque runtime design create correlated errors. The practical constraint is governance latency: enterprises need evaluation signals they can defend to auditors and buyers without rerunning bespoke red-teams for every model or agent release.
macro_patterns.so_what: Model procurement advantage shifts from raw benchmark wins to evaluation stacks that can demonstrate independence, provenance, and reproducibility under continuous model churn.

macro_patterns.name: Context budget triage
macro_patterns.summary: The cost-constrained RAG synthesis cluster, the KV-cache and sparse adaptation cluster, and the adaptive visual tokenization cluster all attack the same systems bottleneck: too much useful evidence exists to read naively, while memory bandwidth and context growth dominate serving cost. Research is converging on query-aware compression, adaptive token allocation, and cache-efficient attention rather than brute-force larger context windows.
macro_patterns.so_what: Serving margin shifts from bigger models and longer windows to systems that decide what not to fetch, store, or encode before generation begins.

macro_patterns.name: Runtime security for compound agents
macro_patterns.summary: The security and jailbreak diagnosis cluster and the agent runtime evaluation cluster are converging on a more realistic threat model: failures emerge across multi-step tool use, external content ingestion, and anonymized traffic rather than in single prompts. The non-research constraint is operational exposure: once agents touch code, email, or enterprise systems, traditional appsec assumptions and existing LLM safety filters stop matching the attack surface.
macro_patterns.so_what: Security control points move from model-level moderation to runtime provenance, state tracking, and action-layer verification across the whole agent stack.

clusters.label: Agent injection diagnostics
clusters.one_line: Research is formalizing where compound LLM and agent systems fail under jailbreaks, indirect prompt injection, and mixed software-hardware attack chains.
clusters.existing_landscape: Lakera, Robust Intelligence, HiddenLayer, Microsoft Prompt Shields, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, Protect AI, and Arthur already cover pieces of LLM security, prompt injection detection, guardrails, and model scanning. Agent frameworks such as LangChain, OpenAI Agents tooling, and Anthropic's tool-use patterns provide execution plumbing, while cloud platforms rely heavily on policy filters and perimeter controls. Across these offerings, the default assumption is still that harmful behavior can be caught at prompt boundaries, model I/O, or static policy checkpoints.
clusters.research_industry_gap: The research is shifting to stateful, cross-turn, and cross-component threat models that today's products only partially expose. TwinGate targets decompositional jailbreaks in anonymized, interleaved traffic; the Four-Checkpoint Framework localizes which stage of the safety pipeline failed; authenticated prompts/context introduces cryptographic provenance; and Cascade shows that compound AI risk spans conventional software and hardware gadgets, not just prompt text. None of the named vendors currently offer a unified runtime view that ties provenance, hidden-state or trajectory monitoring, and downstream action verification across the whole agent execution graph.
clusters.why_now: This is a NEW cluster and one of the clearest accelerations in the corpus. Recent papers sharpen the gap by abandoning toy single-turn attacks for realistic deployment settings: indirect prompt injection competitions, anonymized traffic, and runtime misbehavior detection without access to editable weights.
clusters.risks: Microsoft, NVIDIA, or a specialist such as Lakera could fold stateful prompt provenance and multi-turn attack tracing into existing guardrail platforms. Some papers also depend on deployment access to traces or internals that closed-model APIs do not expose.

clusters.label: Cost-aware evidence synthesis
clusters.one_line: RAG research is moving from top-k retrieval toward query-aware context merging, answer-centric retriever tuning, and explicit trust allocation under tight token budgets.
clusters.existing_landscape: OpenAI File Search, Anthropic retrieval patterns, Cohere Rerank, Pinecone, Weaviate, Elastic, Vespa, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and GraphRAG-style systems already support retrieval, reranking, chunking, and orchestration. Fireworks, Vectara, and enterprise search vendors package production RAG stacks with monitoring and hybrid retrieval. These systems mostly assume the core problem is finding better chunks, then stuffing a bounded number of them into context.
clusters.research_industry_gap: The research is treating retrieval as a constrained synthesis problem rather than a ranking problem. Papers on query-aware context merging, CARROT-style learned cost-constrained retrieval, and answer-centric retriever tuning all imply that relevance scores on isolated chunks are the wrong optimization target when token budget, bridging evidence, and trust in noisy context determine final answer quality. Existing products expose retrievers, rerankers, and context windows, but they rarely expose a first-class control loop for deciding when additional evidence is not worth the latency or token cost, or for composing partial evidence into a minimal answer-sufficient context.
clusters.why_now: Although tagged STABLE, this cluster still has one of the stronger growth ratios in the set. Recent papers such as 'Rethinking Retrieval-Augmentation as Synthesis' and 'Do We Still Need GraphRAG?' sharpen the shift from static retrieval pipelines toward adaptive, sequential evidence allocation.
clusters.risks: This gap can narrow quickly because LangChain, LlamaIndex, Vespa, or OpenAI can add learned budget allocators and synthesis stages as features. Some enterprise buyers will also accept simpler heuristics if they are easier to debug than learned retrieval policies.

clusters.label: Memory-bandwidth-constrained decoding
clusters.one_line: LLM systems research is converging on KV-cache compression, partitionable attention variants, and sparse memory updates to relieve decoding and continual adaptation bottlenecks.
clusters.existing_landscape: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, MLC, Fireworks, Groq, and major GPU clouds already optimize serving with paged attention, quantization, batching, and long-context kernels. LoRA and related PEFT methods dominate practical adaptation, while vendors increasingly advertise larger context windows as a product feature. The shared assumption is that model quality scales acceptably if you compress or page the KV cache and keep adaptation as lightweight parameter deltas.
clusters.research_industry_gap: Several papers point to a deeper systems mismatch: decoding cost is now set by KV-cache movement across HBM-SRAM boundaries and by attention designs that shard poorly under distributed inference. Multi-Head Low-Rank Attention explicitly targets MLA's tensor-parallel bottleneck, and adaptive KV quantization shows fixed-precision cache policies waste bandwidth on unimportant tokens. Shipping systems expose generic cache quantization and serving optimizations, but not architecture-aware allocation policies that adapt cache precision, sharding behavior, or memory updates to token importance and distributed topology.
clusters.why_now: This cluster is STABLE rather than NEW, but the representative papers have become more explicit about the physical bottleneck. The strongest signal is that recent work names off-chip bandwidth and tensor-parallel redundancy, which turns a model optimization topic into an infrastructure constraint.
clusters.risks: vLLM, NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, or a frontier model provider can absorb much of this through kernel and scheduler updates. Some of the gains also require model-architecture changes, which slows adoption in API-driven markets.

clusters.label: Reproducible agent runtime evaluation
clusters.one_line: Research is standardizing how to evaluate software agents under realistic tool use, branching trajectories, and executable environments rather than static task benchmarks.
clusters.existing_landscape: SWE-bench, OpenHands, Devin, Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, LangSmith, Weights & Biases, Braintrust, E2B, and OpenAI/Anthropic eval tooling cover parts of agent benchmarking, trace capture, and software-task evaluation. Most shipped systems still report success rates on curated tasks, often with incomplete disclosure of environment setup, rollback policy, or runtime costs. The common assumption is that benchmark success is portable across toolchains and execution environments.
clusters.research_industry_gap: The papers are pushing evaluation down into the runtime substrate itself. AutoControl Arena uses executable environments to separate logic from narrative; the reproducibility study shows many agentic SE results cannot be reproduced from paper descriptions; and multi-agent collaboration work treats coordination structure, memory isolation, and branching execution as primary experimental variables. Existing tooling captures traces, but it rarely makes environment synthesis, branch accounting, or execution-grounded failure attribution first-class, which means buyers still cannot tell whether an agent improvement came from the model, the tools, or hidden evaluator choices.
clusters.why_now: This cluster remains large and still grew week over week, but the more important signal is qualitative: representative papers have shifted from 'agents can do X' to 'we cannot compare agents unless runtime conditions are executable and disclosed.' That is a real tightening of research consensus.
clusters.risks: LangSmith, OpenAI eval tooling, or the SWE-bench ecosystem can add more rigorous environment provenance and runtime accounting. Also, if the market consolidates around a few dominant agent stacks, buyers may tolerate less rigorous evaluation than the research community wants.

clusters.label: Adaptive visual token allocation
clusters.one_line: Vision-language research is reallocating visual compute dynamically by task, instruction, and spatial salience instead of feeding uniformly dense image or video tokens.
clusters.existing_landscape: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Qwen, and LLaVA-family models already serve multimodal models with some internal token compression, multi-resolution encoders, and video frame sampling. Hardware and inference stacks from NVIDIA and OSS runtimes focus on throughput, while product surfaces still present multimodal inference as essentially fixed-cost per image or clip. The prevailing assumption is that visual encoding is a front-end cost to optimize globally, not a per-query budget decision.
clusters.research_industry_gap: Recent papers such as AdaptVision, iGVLM, and LLMind suggest the model can decide how much of the image to read based on the instruction and can preserve quality by concentrating tokens on task-relevant regions. That matters because multimodal serving is increasingly constrained by visual token explosion and prefill latency, especially for video. Current products expose model choice and input resolution, but they do not expose instruction-conditioned visual acquisition or task-dependent token budgets as a controllable systems primitive.
clusters.why_now: This cluster is not the fastest-growing one, but the representative work is converging on the same idea from different angles: dynamic instruction-guided encoding, foveated training-free representations, and active visual acquisition. That convergence makes the gap more credible than a one-off architecture tweak.
clusters.risks: Frontier multimodal providers can implement these policies internally without exposing them, closing the technical gap while leaving little room for independent platforms. Gains may also be harder to verify externally because closed APIs hide tokenization internals.
